doc.title: Don Alias interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

title: Rick Montalbano and Charles Frichtell
summary: Rowe relays a tribute from Rick Montalbano, whom Alias credits with saving his spirit; they find a shared connection through bassist Charles Frichtell.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well I want to wrap up with — are we going to make it — a quote from a mutual friend.
Lay it on me. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -21-
He said about you, he said “he’s one of the greatest people I’ve ever known, I learned more from him than any other musician I can think of.”

Mmm, yeah, I can’t handle this kind of stuff man. And vice versa. I learned, him being there during that period of time was like he saved my spirit. He saved my spirit, which at one particular time I didn’t think was going to make it. But him being there, he’s one guy that I would go to lengths to do anything for. I’ll give you an example. If Rick called up now and said “hey man I need you up here,” I’d go without even thinking about it.
Glad to hear that. Well I learned a lot from him too actually. So I think in one respect, you must have taught me a few things through him.
We had so much fun. You ought to let him tell you the fun that we used to have. Do you know the bass player Charles Frichtell?
Because when he came from playing with Chuck, when he came on the gig he says “Rick Montalbano told me—” I says “you know Rick Montalbano?” And he knew Rick too. Did you guys play together?
Absolutely. A lot of times. Yup. And now I sub for him.
